question_or_proposition: For Total Suspended Solids at Outfall 001, does the value "50" in the Daily Maximum mg/L discharge-limitations column establish an enforceable numeric discharge limit for compliance comparison, or is TSS monitoring report-only with no applicable numeric limit, given that the 30-Day Average mg/L column shows "Report" and the Standard Units and lbs/day limitation columns show "N/A"?
required_context: Outfall 001 limitations table column headers (Standard Units MINIMUM/MAXIMUM; lbs/day 30-Day Avg and Daily Max; mg/L 30-Day Avg and Daily Max; monitoring frequency and sample type)
Adjacent pollutant rows in the same table that pair "Report" with numeric values or use "N/A" across limitation columns (e.g., Total Copper, Dissolved Copper, Total Hardness)
source_locator: gcc/final_permit.pdf, page 3, section part_i, Outfalls 001 limitations table (Total Suspended Solids row)
notes: The nominated row mixes report-only markers (N/A in Standard Units and lbs/day columns; Report in the mg/L 30-Day Average column) with a numeric value (50) in the mg/L Daily Maximum column. Purpose A turns on distinguishing enforceable numeric limits from report-only monitoring; Purpose C turns on classifying missing or non-numeric TSS evidence. Purpose B appears unaffected because the monitoring frequency (1/Week, Grab) is stated independently in the monitoring-requirements columns.
